Results show that shared components capture patterns that generalise across tasks, while task-specific components provide capacity without increasing model size. Public availability gating further reduces encrypted computation by removing branches determined by publicly known task and owner availability without altering predictions. Overall, CoGITAtion enables gaze model reuse, efficient privacy-preserving deployment, and robust inference under incomplete owner availability while retaining interpretable gaze representations.

papers.title: Quality-Control Policies Shape Model Behaviour in Computational Pathology
papers.abstract: Quality-control policies determine which image regions are used by computational pathology models, but their effects are difficult to isolate when quality estimation and input selection are coupled. We make these policies explicit, configurable and testable. We introduce PathQC-3C, comprising 1,661 densely annotated regions from 1,194 haematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images across 32 cancer/tissue categories, and TileNet, a framework that separates dense tissue/background/artefact estimation from task-specific input-selection policies. We evaluated the default predictor across three held-out cohorts and against harmonised quality-control comparators, assessed policy decisions in a blinded single-pathologist audit, and tested alternative policies in three downstream settings. In retrospective CAMELYON16 multiple-instance learning, background-aware selection improved the pooled out-of-fold area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from 0.758 to 0.839 compared with random sampling from the same exhaustive candidate pool under a fixed tile budget. In weak-label lung classification, strict artefact exclusion reduced the pre-matching candidate pool by approximately 43%, with small metric-dependent differences after matching training-set size and patient contribution. PathQCAug, which composites real artefact components during tumour-stroma model adaptation, improved macro Dice on high-artefact tiles under severe held-out composited artefacts across three training seeds and outperformed random-erasing and clean-tissue controls. Separating quality estimation from policy execution provides an auditable way to control which image content enters computational pathology models; the appropriate policy is task specific, and clinical utility remains to be established.

papers.title: ReSA: Preserving Reference-Specified Foreground in In-Context Segmentation
papers.abstract: In-context segmentation uses annotated references to specify the target and its extent in a query image. Accurately transferring this reference-specified foreground requires recovering target regions while suppressing irrelevant predictions. We propose ReSA, a reference-guided framework that unifies query adaptation and mask selection through a shared reference kernel. ReSA leverages foreground and background reference prototypes to constrain prediction changes during adaptation and guide foreground selection through reference-weighted reconstruction. This shared guidance promotes consistent use of reference information across prediction refinement and mask formation. ReSA further selects among adapted predictions and aligns boundary refinement with the selected foreground threshold. We establish a theoretical bound connecting reference-response changes during adaptation and soft reconstruction. With a frozen visual encoder and lightweight test-time adaptation, ReSA requires no offline task training. Ablation studies demonstrate improved foreground retention and effective suppression of false-positive regions, while qualitative results show more complete masks with fewer isolated artifacts. Across ten object, part, and cross-domain segmentation benchmarks, ReSA achieves the highest average mIoU among the evaluated methods, reaching 62.6% in 1-shot and 71.8% in 5-shot.

papers.title: Characterising stellar photometry with invertible neural networks: Joint inference of stellar parameters and extinction
papers.abstract: We introduce an extension to a simulation-based deep-learning approach for the characterisation of stellar photometry and investigate the feasibility of jointly estimating stellar properties and extinction. We used the PARSEC stellar evolutionary models to train a conditional invertible neural network (cINN) to jointly estimate full posterior distributions of stellar parameters and extinction. We tested our cINN on synthetic data and real Gaia+2MASS photometry of the two star-forming regions Taurus and Upper Scorpius. We compared our predicted extinction maps to two independent catalogues based on Gaia XP-spectra. On synthetic test data, our trained cINN exhibited a good predictive performance, achieving root mean squared errors (RMSEs) for the maximum a posteriori point estimates of about 0.16 mag for $A_V$, 0.07 dex for $\log(T_{eff}/K)$, 0.16 dex for $\log(g/cms^{-2})$, 0.2 dex for $\log(L/L\odot)$ and 0.1 dex for $\log(M_{ini}/M_\odot)$. Only $\log(age/yr)$ has proven harder to constrain with an RMSE of 0.56 dex. On the Gaia+2MASS observations of Taurus and Upper Scorpius, we retrieved reasonable extinction maps, exhibiting structures that are visually consistent with local clouds. Compared to the independent XP-spectra-based extinction studies, we found a good qualitative agreement and recovered the same prominent spatial structures. Quantitatively, however, we identified an average systematic overestimation of extinction in our approach of 0.5-0.7 mag compared to the spectroscopic studies. We investigated these offsets and identified photometric and distance uncertainties, which are currently unaccounted for in our approach, as likely causes. In conclusion, we demonstrated the feasibility of jointly estimating stellar parameters and extinction with our cINN approach, making it a promising avenue to further pursue for robust and efficient analysis of large photometric surveys.

papers.title: A general reduction and explicit remoteness formulas for exact slow 2-Nim
papers.abstract: In exact slow $2$-Nim, a move removes one token from each of two nonempty piles. For any number of piles, we relate Smith remoteness in the exact game to the remoteness $D$ of Moore's slow game on the piles that remain after a largest pile is removed. If the total number of tokens $N$ is odd, the exact game has remoteness $\min(D,\lfloor N/2\rfloor)$. If $N$ is even, its remoteness equals $D$ when $2D\le N$ and is either $N/2$ or $N/2-1$ otherwise. Both values can occur for the same $N$, $D$, and number of piles. We determine $D$ explicitly for five piles. This gives a six-pile remoteness formula and a rule for selecting an optimal move. Both take $O(b)$ bit operations when each pile size has at most $b$ bits. We also give a closed formula for positions with any number of unit piles and two further piles of arbitrary size. For the GM move rule, we prove the proposed descriptions of the exceptions in the four- and five-pile games and give the exact threshold at which a specified six-pile move ceases to be optimal as the largest pile grows. Finally, we classify all outcome-preserving sorted translations for five and six piles.

papers.title: Learning Interaction Dynamics via Motion-Region Guidance for Robotic Video World Models
papers.abstract: Action-conditioned video world models imagine future observations under candidate robot actions, providing a promising visual tool for robot policy evaluation and interaction simulation. However, existing video world models often optimize global reconstruction errors instead of emphasizing interaction-relevant regions. As a result, they may preserve overall scene appearance but overlook local interaction details, leading to physically implausible outcomes such as hallucinated contact effects and inconsistent robot-object interactions. We introduce MoReWorld, a unified motion-region-guided framework that uses a shared motion region, the part of the environment that moves in response to the robot's actions, to focus dynamics learning and video generation on interaction-relevant regions. The same motion region guides local motion prediction, region-aware supervision, and motion-gated future-feature conditioning. At inference time, the motion region is predicted as a motion probability map from visual history and robot actions, without requiring future observations or ground-truth motion labels. On WorldSimProbe, MoReWorld achieves the highest overall simulator-faithfulness score, with the strongest performance on local consistency, global consistency, and interaction dynamics. These results indicate that motion-region guidance helps the model preserve scene-level consistency while more faithfully predicting action-conditioned interaction dynamics.

papers.title: A local symmetry forces positivity for projectively induced Kahler-Einstein metrics
papers.abstract: We prove that a projectively induced Kahler-Einstein metric has positive Einstein constant as soon as it admits one nonzero local real-holomorphic Killing field. Neither completeness nor a prescribed global group action is assumed. This gives a partial answer, under a local symmetry hypothesis, to the general positivity problem for Kahler-Einstein submanifolds of (finite-dimensional) projective space. The key observation is that, by Calabi rigidity, a local real-holomorphic Killing field is induced by a projective unitary vector field whose tangency propagates along any connected global Kahler immersion, without a simple-connectivity assumption. Applied to Hulin's complete continuation, this produces a global Killing field with a bounded Hamiltonian potential given by the ambient projective moment map. The resulting Laplace equation, the Omori--Yau maximum principle and Yau's Liouville theorem exclude both negative and zero Einstein curvature. We also prove a non-Einstein obstruction under uniformly negative Ricci curvature and obtain compact equivariant continuations.

papers.title: Dual-Agent DRL based Cooperative Beamforming and Trajectory Optimization for UAV-ISAC Networks
papers.abstract: This paper considers a low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) network, where multiple ground base stations (BSs) provide integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) services for multiple communication UAVs (C-UAVs) and sensing UAVs (S-UAVs). With the objective of maximizing the average sum rate of C-UAVs over the entire flight episode, we jointly optimize the multi-BS multi-UAV ISAC beamforming and trajectory design, subject to the BS transmit power budget and the sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints of S-UAVs, as well as the flight mission and collision avoidance constraints of C-UAVs and S-UAVs. Based on the multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) technique, we develop a dual-agent scheme, termed DeepDA-OPT, to solve the resulting constrained Markov decision process (MDP). In the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme, two agents, i.e., Agent-B and Agent-T, are specifically deployed for learning the multi-BS ISAC transmit beamformers and the C-UAV/S-UAV trajectories, respectively, where the optimal BS receive beamformers for the sensing echo signals of S-UAVs are obtained in closed form by leveraging the generalized Rayleigh quotient theorem. To mitigate the overestimation of value functions, both Agent-B and Agent-T are trained based on the twin-delayed deep deterministic (TD3) policy-gradient algorithm. In addition, a constraint-aware noise exploration policy is employed, and the reward function is designed to incorporate a sensing penalty and a flight urgency penalty, thereby guiding the training of Agent-B and Agent-T. Numerical results show that, compared with the baseline schemes, the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme achieves a higher average sum rate of C-UAVs, while the sensing SINR constraints are empirically well satisfied and no collision violation is observed under the evaluated settings.

papers.title: A Validation-Driven Bilevel Optimization Method for Mesh-Free PDE Solvers and Its Error Analysis
papers.abstract: Mesh-free partial differential equation (PDE) solvers construct discrete systems from residuals at sampled points. These solvers fit coefficients in a parameterized trial representation and select solver-design parameters governing the representation, training-residual weighting, and regularization. These parameters strongly affect solution accuracy, yet existing selection strategies are largely tailored to particular solver classes. To address this limitation, we formulate a unified validation-driven bilevel optimization framework applicable across different solver classes, in which the lower level fits coefficients using training collocation residuals, while the upper level selects solver-design parameters using held-out validation residuals. For nonlinear PDEs, however, solving the nonlinear lower-level problem to high accuracy is costly, while the adjoint system is typically ill-conditioned and indefinite. To address this issue, we propose an efficient implicit hypergradient method that approximates the lower-level response using finite, warm-started damped Gauss-Newton (GN) updates. For the adjoint solve, we use the damped GN matrix to compute an initial adjoint and to precondition a finite number of minimum residual iterations. To quantify the errors introduced by these approximations, we derive local hypergradient error bounds that separate the contributions of the finite lower-level solve, adjoint damping, and the final adjoint residual. Combining this analysis with validation sampling bounds and residual stability, we relate validation residuals to PDE solution accuracy and establish error bounds for the computed PDE solution. Numerical experiments on several nonlinear PDEs, including a high-dimensional problem, demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method across Kansa, random feature and extreme learning machine, and physics-informed neural network solvers.

papers.title: Breaking the Long Horizon: Short-Horizon Process Supervision for Long-Form Generation in LLMs
papers.abstract: Long-form generation is increasingly important for agentic LLM systems, yet current reinforcement learning methods typically optimize an entire document with a single outcome-level reward. This delayed and coarse-grained supervision makes it difficult to localize errors and assign credit across semantically distinct parts of the output. To address this, we propose a short-horizon framework that reformulates long-form generation through semantic decomposition into segment-level decisions. Each segment is generated with prefix-conditioned context, allowing cross-segment coherence to be preserved while keeping supervision local. The generated segments are then scored with rubric-based rewards for adherence, coherence, and relevance, enabling explicit local supervision at the segment level. These local rewards are used to compute step-wise advantages, yielding localized policy updates. To isolate the effect of supervision granularity, we instantiate both outcome-level supervision and our short-horizon process reward method (SH-PRM) under the same GRPO framework. Across multiple LLMs and two long-form generation benchmarks, SH-PRM consistently outperforms outcome-level supervision and strong inference-time baselines under the same optimizer and comparable budgets. Further analyses suggest that these gains primarily arise from improved credit assignment. Overall, our results suggest that aligning supervision granularity with the semantic structure of long-form generation is an effective design principle for long-form LLM training.

papers.title: EcomWriteBench: A Real-World Benchmark for E-commerce Writing Tasks
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used throughout e-commerce workflows to generate content that informs purchasing decisions and supports customer interactions. Evaluating these systems requires accounting for user needs, product evidence, structural constraints, and business requirements that are not fully captured by general-purpose writing benchmarks. We introduce EcomWriteBench, a real-world benchmark containing 3,861 queries from 69 e-commerce writing tasks across 13 categories and five languages. Through task-level extraction, cross-task consolidation, and refinement guided by human feedback, EcomWriteBench constructs a shared pool of 37 abilities and identifies the subset applicable to each task. Ability-wise scoring enables us to compare state-of-the-art LLMs on EcomWriteBench and characterize their relative strengths and weaknesses across fine-grained e-commerce writing abilities. We further propose a preference-calibrated weight-learning framework that converts human pairwise preferences into interpretable scoring rubrics through global, category-level, and task-level aggregation weights. This framework provides a reusable approach for translating human preferences into automated evaluation by combining ability discovery, ability-wise scoring, and preference-calibrated aggregation, and can potentially be applied to a broad range of benchmarks beyond EcomWriteBench. On held-out queries, our scoring framework achieves 88.96% agreement with human preferences, compared with 78.54% for conventional LLM-as-a-judge scoring.

papers.title: GRACE: Controlled Evidence Interventions for Diagnosing and Improving Knowledge Integration in GraphRAG
papers.abstract: GraphRAG combines a language model's parametric knowledge with retrieved graph evidence, yet aggregate accuracy cannot show whether failures stem from missing paths, distractors, or conflicts with model knowledge. We introduce GRACE, a benchmark built by executing LC-QuAD 2.0 queries over Wikidata and applying four controlled interventions to each evidence subgraph: severing a support path, adding type-compatible distractors, attaching high-degree hubs, and replacing the supported answer with a counterfactual entity. Questions and option positions remain fixed across the five states. The validated benchmark contains 4,028 questions and 20,140 question-graph pairs. These comparisons reveal that question-only routing cannot distinguish evidence states, while relevance guidance can improve answerable states yet hurt when the support path is severed: relevant facts may not jointly suffice to answer. We propose QCFSE-SA, which combines typed local attention, global graph attention, and question-conditioned evidence guidance with a calibrated graph-support gate. With the factual context and generator held fixed, it improves controlled-state accuracy from 57.17% to 62.78% (+5.61 points; question-clustered 95% CI [+5.04, +6.17]) and broken-state accuracy from 55.41% to 67.85%. Over-abstention on semantic distractors remains an open challenge.

papers.title: A 3D PINN-Based Framework for Patient-Specific Pulmonary Hemodynamics Using Windkessel Models
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular fluid dynamics modeling relies heavily on mesh-based numerical methods such as Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). While accurate, these methods entail significant computational costs and complex meshing workflows that limit their translation to clinical practice. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are a promising meshless alternative that embeds the governing equations directly into neural network training. In this work, we propose a PINN framework for pulsatile blood flow in patient-specific geometries with dynamic lumped-parameter Windkessel (RCR) outlet conditions representing distal vascular impedance. Coupling the Windkessel ODE to a 3D network raises two difficulties: the ODE alone does not fix the pressure level, and the local pressure variations that drive the flow are orders of magnitude smaller than the basal pressure imposed by the outlet. We address them by decomposing pressure into a time-dependent basal part and a spatially varying part, an initial condition and gauge for the Windkessel equation, a global mass-balance constraint, and a periodic Fourier embedding of time. Validated on 2D canonical channels (steady and pulsatile, with and without RCR outlet), the framework is then applied to a patient-specific right pulmonary artery, reproducing outlet flow, mean pressure, and the velocity and dynamic pressure fields with errors on the order of the data resolution. Finally, we solve the inverse problem of identifying the three Windkessel parameters of the outlet from synthetic data, recovering them with errors of about 0.3% from deliberately wrong initial values. Residual biases in the local pressure field and the need to test robustness to noisy clinical data remain open, but the results support PINNs as complementary tools for meshless hemodynamics and patient-specific digital twins.

papers.title: PAVE: A Harness for Geometrically Consistent Road Network Modeling with Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Transportation models, whether they simulate traffic or support planning, are only as reliable as the road networks they run on, down to the lanes and turns at each intersection. Practitioners still take such a network from GIS files and supply its junction and movement data by hand, a task that recurs with each new base year and design alternative, or they generate it from open map data. OpenStreetMap's lane tags give the correct layout for only 13 of the 44 approaches we test; open map data are often incomplete or inaccurate. Satellite and street-level imagery, in contrast, cover all 44 and show their lanes as painted. Vision-language models (VLMs) can read such imagery, but asked directly they lose geometric consistency when the same lane must be matched across a satellite crop, street-level photos taken from different poses and an ID-labelled network. We therefore present PAVE (Perceive, Anchor, Verify, Edit), a harness in which code measures what can be measured, traffic engineering knowledge enters as general rules and checks, and the model makes only the open judgements, each anchored to network IDs so that checks catch answers that contradict a measurement, a second reading or a traffic rule. Scored against human labels at signalised intersections, PAVE raises the share of exactly correct lane layouts from 49-64% with a single request to 86-91% for two VLMs, with most of the gain coming from reading one approach at a time on traced lanes. The same division of work edits a real network to a planning brief: the model names the links and nodes of each part of a facility, and code builds the edit from a design template. Of 18 edits, 16 pass every network check, against none when the model writes its own code, and 2 contain a design or coding error, against 7. An analysis shows where VLMs lose geometric consistency and which check catches each failure.

papers.title: WaXup: Weight Averaging of Experts as Data Augmentation for Robust Introspection
papers.abstract: As the capabilities of large language models keep improving, traditional mechanistic interpretability methods struggle to keep pace. In contrast, trainable introspection methods emerge as a promising alternative; they repurpose the model itself as a self-diagnostic tool, trained to verbalize what it has learned during finetuning in natural language. While training on datasets of finetuned experts achieves encouraging results, it currently lacks robustness and generalization. Building on the data augmentation framework of MiXup, we introduce WaXup, a method that augments the introspection training set through linear interpolation in the weight space. This is motivated by the linear mode connectivity property: weight averaged experts interpolate the behaviors of the initial experts. We evaluate WaXup on three benchmarks: hidden-behavior models, a meta-dataset of real-world NLP tasks and AuditBench, a challenging alignment auditing suite of models adversarially trained to conceal their behaviors. WaXup improves the accuracy of generated descriptions as well as robustness to various distribution shifts. We hope to improve the reliability of trainable introspection methods towards better and safer models.

papers.title: Vanishing bond-percolation threshold implies vanishing contact-process threshold
papers.abstract: We show that for any infinite, locally finite and connected graph $G$ and $p\in(0,1/2]$ the survival probability of the contact process with infection rate $λ\ge20p$ is at least $3/4$ times the bond percolation probability with retention probability $p$. In particular, $λ_c(G)\le20\,p_c(G)$ whenever $p_c(G)<1/2$, and $p_c(G)=0$ implies $λ_c(G)=0$. The proof uses a submartingale built from percolation clusters on finite balls. We contrast this with the SIR epidemic, in which every vertex is infected at most once, and for which there are graphs with $p_c(G)=0$ on which the SIR epidemic dies out almost surely for every infection rate.

papers.title: Show Me the Answer: Visual Grounding on Dashboards
papers.abstract: Natural language interaction has become an increasingly important paradigm for accessing complex visual information systems. In visual data analytics environments, such as dashboards, a key capability is to ground user queries to specific visual elements, enabling systems to identify the visual evidence relevant to the query. However, existing visual grounding research has primarily focused on natural images, while grounding in dashboards remains underexplored due to their complex multi-chart layouts and fine-grained visual elements. In this paper, we study the task of Visual Grounding on Dashboards (VGD): Given a dashboard screenshot and a natural language query, the goal is to localize the visual element corresponding to the query using a bounding box. We propose VGD-Net, a two-stage grounding framework that reflects how users typically locate information in dashboards, by first performing query-aware chart retrieval and then fine-grained in-chart grounding. To systematically evaluate VGD-Net's performance on this task, we construct VGD-Bench, a benchmark specifically designed for VGD, covering three complementary settings: chart retrieval, in-chart grounding, and overall VGD. Experimental results show that our two-stage VGD-Net outperforms strong multimodal baselines on the VGD task, achieving a mean IoU of 57.06 and a success rate of 66.82, while also delivering superior performance over existing methods in both stages of chart retrieval and in-chart grounding. These results highlight the value of stage decomposition for reliable and interpretable VGD, and its potential to support query-driven visual analysis.

papers.title: Interplay of elliptical laser polarization and scattering geometry in laser-assisted pair production of doubly charged Higgs bosons in the Higgs Triplet Model
papers.abstract: We study the pair production of a doubly charged Higgs boson via $e^{-} e^{+}$ in the presence of a polarized laser field in the Higgs Triplet Model (HTM), mediated by the photon and the $Z$ boson exchange. A unified formulation based on generalized Bessel functions is developed for a monochromatic plane wave with arbitrary ellipticity, encompassing linear, circular, and elliptical polarization states. The numerical analysis shows a strong interplay between laser polarization and scattering geometry, affecting both the characteristic multiphoton domain and the relative strengths of individual harmonic contributions. At a fixed cycle-averaged squared laser potential, the peak ratio normalized to linear polarization exhibits distinct geometry-dependent trends, including a reversal of the polarization hierarchy between different incidence configurations. The dependence on the collision energy and doubly charged Higgs boson mass is also investigated, revealing pronounced kinematic effects on the differential cross section. In contrast, the relative polarization pattern remains similar over a broad mass range. These results provide a unified characterization of polarization and geometrical effects on the multiphoton structure of this process.

papers.title: Network Traffic Dynamics in Urban Low-Altitude Air Transport with Projected-Space Macroscopic Fundamental Diagrams
papers.abstract: The growth of Low-Altitude Air Transport (LAAT) systems calls for effective macroscopic modeling tools to manage dense drone traffic. The Macroscopic Fundamental Diagram (MFD) offers a promising framework for this purpose, but its conventional formulations do not directly account for the three-dimensional interactions and path deviations that characterize drone operations. To address this challenge, we introduce a projected-space framework that represents drone motion using projected speed and shortest origin-destination (OD) distances, eliminating the dependence on realized trip lengths that are unknown at trip generation. Under suitable assumptions, we prove the steady-state exactness of the projected-space accumulation-based model and establish deterministic finite-window error bounds for the trip-based estimator. The projected-space accumulation-based formulation is further extended to heterogeneous multi-class systems to accommodate different drone characteristics and operational priorities. Microscopic simulations validate the projected-space formulations under stationary and transient traffic conditions, including hysteresis. Moreover, simulations involving heterogeneous priority classes demonstrate that mixed-priority operations can improve network outflow under the investigated scenarios. These findings establish a theoretical foundation for projected-space macroscopic modeling of LAAT systems and support its application to real-time traffic estimation and future airspace management and control.

papers.title: How Meandering Flow Sculpts Ice
papers.abstract: Ice-water phase change subject to a mean flow widely exists in the Cryosphere, with implications on glacier evolution, human transportation, flooding events, etc. Understanding the relevant phase change dynamics requires identifying the roles of shear and rotation due to the mean flow. Combining experiments, numerical simulations and theoretical modelling, we reveal the combined effects of shear and rotation on the coupled dynamics of water flow, heat transfer and phase change in an annular system. Increasing shear and rotation drive a stronger secondary circulation which significantly enhances global heat transfer and redistributes the radial heat flux, and eventually lead to a thinner equilibrium ice layer and a larger ice thickness difference in the radial direction. Further, we develop an integral thermal balance model that explains the mean ice thickness through estimating the additional heat transfer, and a local thermal balance model that explains the inner-outer ice thickness difference by relating it to the non-uniform convective heat flux. The local model shows qualitative agreement with field measurements when applied to an ice-covered meandering river. These results contribute to understanding the common physical mechanism for ice-water phase change under shear and rotation, offering a theoretical basis for explaining and predicting ice evolution in meandering rivers among other relevant scenarios.

papers.title: Trotter Error Bounds in Lean 4 with a Cancellation-Aware Analysis of the Fourth-Order Suzuki Formula
papers.abstract: We formalize the commutator-scaling bound of Childs et al. in Lean 4. For skew-adjoint generators, the local order condition gives an explicit integer step count sufficient to meet a prescribed error tolerance. We apply the theorem in Lean to the binary fourth-order Suzuki formula. For this formula we can also account for cancellation within and between steps. Using local remainder estimates of Casas and Murua, we sum the signed quintic and centered seventh-degree error terms after conjugating each to the interaction picture. For every positive integer step count, we bound the difference between this sum and the global error operator. At fixed time the explicit remainder is eighth order in the step size, and the integral of the conjugated quintic term gives the exact leading error coefficient. The Lean proofs cover the two-generator finite-sum estimates, including the spectral norm for complex matrices. On five ten-site nearest-neighbor Heisenberg instances at time $10$ and tolerance $10^{-3}$, the transported sum meets the tolerance at a mean of $129.4$ steps. Taking a separate norm at each step with the same polynomial and remainder gives a mean first crossing between $184.6$ and $185.2$ steps. The accumulated Casas--Murua local bound at $q=8$ gives a mean of $184.8$ steps.

papers.title: Borrow the Style, Follow the Prompt: Progressive Reference-Guided Stylization
papers.abstract: Reference-guided text-to-image stylization transfers visual appearance to content specified by text, but the reference subjects and backgrounds can interfere with what the generated image depicts. Suppressing this unwanted information can also discard transferable texture and material cues, creating a tension between content control and faithful preservation of the reference style. Accordingly, we propose ProStyle, which learns a content-suppressed style prior through cross-content supervision on same-style pairs with different subjects and backgrounds and injects it with weak conditioning at auxiliary layers to strengthen style expression. Building on this prior, a complementary pathway learns residual corrections from full reference patch features with the content-suppressed style pathway frozen, before both pathways undergo joint refinement under the same objective. For cross-content learning and evaluation, we introduce ReConStyle, which provides 134K training pairs, two test settings, and object-level measures of target-content fidelity and reference-object overlap alongside style similarity and text alignment. ProStyle outperforms all compared SD1.5-based baselines and achieves the best average rank of 1.86 across four automatic and three human-evaluation criteria on ReConStyle-Full. In the user study, it substantially outperforms the baselines in text alignment and combined suitability, with selection rates of 84.36% and 50.90%, respectively. On the external Style-Rank benchmark, it also achieves the highest CLIP-Text and ImageReward scores.

papers.title: Gradient-based optimization of buoyancy distributions for lazy-wave risers
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel gradient-based approach for optimizing the buoyancy distribution of lazy-wave offshore risers. The static response is modeled with a total potential energy formulation for a geometrically nonlinear, inextensible beam on an elastic seabed. The total potential energy is discretized by finite differences and the resulting nonlinear equilibrium system is solved by a two stage continuation procedure, in which the line length and then the buoyancy load are increased incrementally, with Newton--Raphson iterations and an Armijo line search. The design variables are the uplift ratios at the nodes where buoyancy modules may be installed. The optimization minimizes a quadratic measure of buoyancy demand subject to constraints on the maximum curvature and effective tension. The gradients of the constraints are computed by means of a discrete adjoint sensitivity analysis. Three design parametrizations are compared: a continuous formulation with independent nodal uplift ratios, a grouped formulation with fixed module assignments, and a formulation inspired by discrete material optimization that simultaneously selects the uplift ratios of a small catalog of module types and their placement along the riser. The latter yields practical designs with a limited number of module sizes. The framework provides a flexible and computationally efficient tool for preliminary design of lazy-wave configurations.

papers.title: NormFlowSDE: Normalizing Flows for Amortized Bayesian State Estimation
papers.abstract: Bayesian state estimators, such as Kalman filters, estimate states from noisy observations based on dynamical models. However, obtaining accurate models can be challenging when the system involves effects that are difficult to model faithfully, such as friction, impacts, and deformation in contact-rich manipulation. Uncertainty in system parameters, inputs, and disturbances, together with simplified noise models, can further introduce simulation-to-reality mismatch and degrade estimation accuracy. These limitations motivate learning a distribution over state trajectories conditioned on observations and controls without explicitly specifying the underlying physical models. We introduce NormFlowSDE, an amortized Bayesian state estimator that learns a distribution over state trajectories by combining neural stochastic differential equations with conditional normalizing flows. Its key design choice is to utilize the capability of normalizing flows to learn stochastic behavior of variables, while leveraging the continuous-time dynamics of SDEs to model the evolution of states over time. Once trained, the model draws state paths for new measurement sequences without per-sequence optimization. In addition, we connect NormFlowSDE to stochastic continuous-time dynamics by proving weak convergence of a mean-centered, drift-corrected inference scheme to an Itô diffusion under stated assumptions. Finally, we benchmark NormFlowSDE against direct estimators and learned particle filters based on normalizing flows on partially observed dynamical systems, including simulated systems and real-world robot datasets. The results show that NormFlowSDE attains the lowest estimation error with calibrated uncertainty intervals on both robot datasets and filters four times faster than the fastest particle filter on every dataset.

papers.title: Mass Spectra and Radiative Decay Widths of \(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^+\), \(D_{s1}(2460)^+\) and \(D'_{s1}(2536)^+\)
papers.abstract: Inspired by recent experimental reports on the radiative decay \(D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}γ\) and the branching-fraction ratio \(\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}γ]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{+}γ]\), we investigate the mass spectra and radiative decay widths of \(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^+\), \(D_{s1}(2460)^+\) and \(D_{s1}'(2536)^+\). Within the chiral quark model combined with the Gaussian Expansion Method, the mass spectra obtained agree reasonably well with the experimental data. Besides, the branching-fraction ratio obtained in this work is \(\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}γ]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{+}γ] = 0.57\) and \(Γ(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}γ) = 3.80\,\mathrm{keV}\). By analyzing our theoretical results against the latest experimental measurements, we conclude that the \(D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\) can be treated as a mixed state of \(1^1P_1\) and \(1^3P_1\), and it may contain both the \(c\bar{s}\) component and the tetraquark component. In addition, we also obtain \(Γ(D'_{s1}(2536)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}γ) = 9.14\,\mathrm{keV}\) and \(Γ(D'_{s1}(2536)^{+}\to D_s^{+}γ) = 8.59\,\mathrm{keV}\) by treating \(D'_{s1}(2536)^+\) as a meson state. More precise experimental data are required to pin down the internal structure of these states.

papers.title: Optimizing MHz X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy with burst-mode free-electron laser operation
papers.abstract: Burst-mode X-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs) provide a powerful platform for X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS) experiments with sub-microsecond temporal resolution, but the achievable performance is constrained in practice by both photon statistics and the sample's dose tolerance. Here, we develop an analytical framework for estimating the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of pulsed XPCS measurements, including pulse-to-pulse fluctuations of the incident intensity. We combine this description with dose constraints and show that, for a fixed maximum dose, acquiring fewer frames at higher per-pulse intensity yields a higher SNR than distributing the dose over a larger number of low-intensity frames. The framework is validated against measurements at the European XFEL, where the intensity fluctuations of the investigated operation mode are found to cause only a negligible reduction in SNR. We further introduce and experimentally demonstrate a rolling bunch pattern with three pulses per train and variable pulse spacings. This scheme enables more than an order-of-magnitude increase in the accessible per-pulse intensity while maintaining equilibrium dynamics. Our results provide practical guidelines for optimizing dose-efficient MHz-XPCS experiments and for evaluating future XFEL operation modes.

papers.title: Machine-learning-assisted photon pairing for neutral-pion reconstruction at future Higgs factories
papers.abstract: Neutral-pion ($π^0$) reconstruction is important for precision measurements at high-energy colliders, particularly in flavor, $τ$, and Higgs physics. We study $π^0$ candidate selection in four benchmark physics processes at electron--positron colliders, comparing an optimized diphoton mass-window (MW) baseline with four machine-learning methods: a boosted decision tree (BDT), a multilayer perceptron (MLP), ParticleNet (PN), and Particle Transformer (ParT). Performance is evaluated using the product of selection efficiency and purity. At the reference ECAL energy resolution, all four machine-learning methods outperform MW. PN and ParT achieve relative improvements of 53%--95% and 60%--128%, respectively, primarily through better rejection of incorrectly matched photon pairs. Their performance advantage is maintained across the investigated ECAL energy resolutions. Training-sample-size scans reveal two periods of rapid performance improvement separated by slower growth in most PN and ParT learning curves. The improved candidate selection provides a starting point for further studies of $ρ$ and hadronic $τ$ reconstruction.

papers.title: WePM: Hierarchical Conflict Reconciliation for Unified MLLMs
papers.abstract: Bringing multimodal intelligence from the cloud to users' devices keeps sensitive data local and reduces inference cost, but deploying a specialized model per capability duplicates vision-language capacity under tight memory and compute budgets. We formalize heterogeneous capability density (HCD), measuring how broadly and effectively a model serves heterogeneous task families per unit of resident inference memory. High HCD across representation, generation, and decision raises two challenges: these capabilities need visual evidence at different spatial granularities under a fixed token budget, and separately collected task corpora yield conflicting updates to shared parameters, while cross-task paired supervision is costly and ambiguous for open-ended inputs. We present WePM, a family of pocket models unifying representation, generation, and decision within one vision-language backbone. Multi-Granularity Visual Budgeting (MGVB) allocates a fixed visual-token budget across global, regional, and fine-grained banks; Unified Listwise Knowledge Distillation (ULKD) enriches separately collected data with soft teacher guidance, avoiding cross-task paired annotation; Stable and Efficient Multitask Optimization (SEMO) regulates each task's contribution through explicit loss weights and exposure schedules, with sequential gradient accumulation under memory constraints. In the joint representation-generation setting, WePM outperforms all baselines across five evaluation groups, raising the Joint score from 38.15 to 52.74. In single-task evaluation, WePM-4B attains the best average score over 30 embedding, 39 generation, and seven typed-decision benchmarks (72.86, 62.41, 61.11). Against the separate-model stack with the highest HCD, WePM achieves slightly higher balanced performance with 61.9% less resident weight memory, a 2.64-fold higher HCD.

papers.title: Linear Convergence of Adaptive Accelerated Gradient Methods: A Unified Framework
papers.abstract: We establish a unified Lyapunov framework for adaptive accelerated gradient methods on smooth, strongly convex objectives. Conditions on local curvature, stepsize ratios, and coefficient variation ensure eventual linear convergence without assuming stepsize convergence. We verify these conditions for specified AdaNAG-G, smooth unconstrained AC-FGM, and AdaAGM policies and use them to design VC-FG and CC-FG. The verified adaptive main iterations require neither global smoothness nor strong-convexity parameters and avoid restart and backtracking. The framework also sharpens a fixed-step FISTA/NAG-type bound. Experiments on four smooth, strongly convex problem families illustrate complementary performance of the new methods.

papers.title: Adaptive Multiset Tree Tensor Networks for Large-Scale Exciton Dynamics
papers.abstract: Electronic excitations coupled to vibrational environments play an important role in charge and energy transport in molecular materials. Multiset tree tensor networks provide an efficient ansatz for the dynamics of such systems by allowing different electronic configurations to develop independent environmental correlations. However, typical implementations use fixed bond dimensions, significantly limiting the accessible system size and hence their predictive capabilities for large scale systems. To overcome these limitations, we introduce the adaptive multiset tree tensor network (AMTTN) approach, in which the bond dimensions of each configuration are adapted independently using a local energy variance based expansion scheme. Additionally, configurations can be temporarily frozen whenever they are predicted to remain weakly populated throughout a timestep. For the one-dimensional Holstein model, AMTTN reproduces converged exciton dynamics one to two orders of magnitude faster than fixed bond dimension multiset methods, with the dominant cost determined by the dynamically active region with only weak residual dependence on the lattice size. For a P3HT:PCBM heterojunction, it enables simulations of a model containing 52 oligothiophene units avoiding finite size effects occurring on dynamically relevant time scales, which lead to the previously studied 13 unit model substantially overestimating long time populations of bound charge separated states. Our results show that AMTTN provides a practical method for obtaining converged quantum dynamics simulations of challenging excitonic and non-adiabatic systems for which conventional multiset approaches are prohibitively expensive.

papers.title: Regularizing gravity in the presence of matter fields
papers.abstract: We investigate how matter fields affect spacetime regularity in a class of gravitational theories with second-order field equations in spherical symmetry, of which general relativity is a special case, and which may encode effective corrections from an underlying quantum theory of gravity. Focusing on spherically symmetric black holes and cosmological spacetimes in theories in which vacuum spacetimes display bounded curvature invariants, we derive the conditions under which regular geometries can be supported by static and perturbative scalar fields, electromagnetic fields, and radiation fluids. We discuss the impact of matter on the regularity requirements of curvature boundedness and geodesic completeness relative to vacuum, finding in general that coupling to matter does not eliminate the existence of theories with regular solutions.

papers.title: Testing for Coordination Failures in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Deep parallel cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (CMARL)} trains multiple agents that all act at every time step to optimize a common objective. Like single-agent RL, CMARL can produce unsafe behaviors that violate implicit safety requirements not captured by the reward, and these behaviors are hard to explain. However, testing CMARL policies for safety has received less attention than the safety testing of single-agent RL policies. In this paper, we propose DisQ, a test case selection method that identifies failure-revealing states in value-based CMARL by exploiting a signal specific to trained Q-learning agents. The signal is the Q-value gap, an explainable metric that flags a state when the agents' estimates of the achievable return diverge by more than a calibrated threshold. DisQ selects such states for execution and skips those without a gap. Our experiments in four CMARL benchmark environments show that, in most of the evaluated configurations, DisQ improves failure detection over single-agent RL testing methods applied to CMARL, namely random testing and search-based testing with genetic algorithms. Our main contributions are the Q-value gap, an indicator of potential miscoordination computable from a single state without executing the system, and DisQ, a test case selection method that adapts existing single-agent testing methods to CMARL.

papers.title: AMARIS: Merging Generalist and Specialist LLMs via Adaptive Subspace Inheritance
papers.abstract: Domain specialization of large language models (LLMs) often improves target-domain performance but degrades broad capabilities. Model merging is an attractive training-free alternative, yet common parameter-space strategies (for example, interpolation and sparsified averaging) provide limited control over task-specific interference. We introduce Adaptive Model Alignment via Ranked Inherited Subspaces (AMARIS), a covariance-driven framework that transfers specialist updates only along selected activation directions. AMARIS formulates merging as budgeted subspace inheritance: it seeks high specialist activation capture under a regularized base-output perturbation budget, then builds a low-rank projection gate from ranked generalized eigendirections. This yields a single static merged checkpoint that concentrates transfer in high-utility, low-interference directions. We evaluate AMARIS on Qwen3-based merges (8B and 32B) across finance, instruction-following, and multilingual SEA specialization. In our evaluated settings, AMARIS reaches Pareto operating points that are competitive with strong training-free baselines, including 98.37% specialist retention with 95.16% core retention for the 8B finance setting, 103.55% core retention with 90.28% specialist retention for the 8B instruction-following setting, and 99.20% core retention with 94.80% specialist retention for the 32B SEA setting. These results support subspace-constrained merging as a practical route to compositional capability integration without additional training.

papers.title: On the Laugesen--Siudeja Conjecture: A Sharp Lower Bound and Failure of the Upper Bound
papers.abstract: We prove the sharp lower bound in the Laugesen--Siudeja conjecture and give a counterexample to its upper bound. For every bounded convex planar domain, the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $λ_1$, the area $A$, and the centroidal polar moment of inertia $I$ satisfy $λ_1A^3/I>9π^2/2$. The constant is approached by thin isosceles triangles. The lower bound follows from a rectangle comparison in the principal directions of the covariance matrix and a planar random-triangle inequality. For the upper bound, we exhibit an isosceles trapezoid on which $λ_1A^3/I>12π^2$, using Temple's inequality and exact arithmetic.

papers.title: Balanced Boolean Functions from Sparse Niho-Type Permutation Polynomials: Few-Valued Walsh Spectra and Applications
papers.abstract: We study balanced Boolean functions parameterized by two-to-one mappings of the forms $P(x+x^2)$ and $P(x+x^{-1})$, where $P$ is a sparse permutation polynomial with generalized Niho-type exponents. First, for $q=2^m$ with $m$ even, we determine the complete four-valued Walsh distribution of the balanced Boolean function parameterized by $Q(x+x^2)$, where $Q(x)=x(1+x^{q-1}+x^{2(q-1)})$. We then generalize a permutation polynomial studied by Gupta and Sharma to the parameterized family $P_λ(x)=x^{3q-1}+λx^{2q}+λx^2$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. We prove that $P_λ$ is a permutation polynomial if and only if either $λ=0$, or $λ\ne0$ and $X^3+X+λ^{-1}$ has no root in $\mathbb{F}_q$. Moreover, the number of admissible parameters is $(q+2)/3$ when $m$ is even and $(q+4)/3$ when $m$ is odd. Thus, admissible parameters exist for every $m\geq2$, and approximately one-third of the elements of $\mathbb{F}_q$ yield permutation polynomials. For every admissible parameter $λ$, we determine the complete Walsh distribution of the balanced Boolean function $f_λ$ parameterized by $P_λ(x+x^2)$ and prove that this distribution is independent of $λ$. For $m\geq3$, these functions have the five-valued Walsh spectrum ${q,0,-q,-2q,-3q}$, while for $m=2$ the spectrum degenerates to four values. As applications, their supports yield projective minimal binary five-weight codes, sets with five hyperplane intersection numbers, and regular cubelike Cayley graphs with six distinct eigenvalues. Finally, for mappings of the form $P(x+x^{-1})$, we construct an infinite family of balanced Boolean functions with simple explicit trace representations.

papers.title: ReActWAM: Action-Consistent Caching for Efficient World-Action Models
papers.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) often generate future visual states alongside robot actions, introducing substantial computational overhead during inference. During closed-loop execution, consecutive inference cycles often predict similar action sequences, leading to redundant computation. However, reducing this redundancy requires distinguishing consistent actions from changes that demand fresh computation. To address these challenges, we propose ReActWAM, a training-free framework that combines action-intent-guided prefix skipping with inner-chunk prediction reuse. A coarse-to-fine assessment evaluates motion changes, visual consistency, and action prediction conflicts. For eligible chunks, we draw on first-step differences to adapt the cached latent and network features to the current condition, providing an estimate at a later denoising step that bypasses the redundant prefix. Subsequent inference refines this estimate while reusing stable denoising predictions within the chunk. Experiments across LingBot-VA, FastWAM and the Cosmos family on LIBERO-Long and RoboTwin 2.0 demonstrate $1.41\times$--$5.44\times$ GPU inference speedup, with minimal degradation in task success rates. Real-world experiments on a Franka Research 3 (FR3) robot further achieve $1.46\times$ end-to-end speedup while maintaining success rate.

papers.title: GeoSDF-Diff: Geometry-Aware Diffusion Planning for Collision-Free Trajectories
papers.abstract: Diffusion models have recently attracted increasing attention in motion planning due to their ability to model high-dimensional and multi-modal trajectory distributions. However, existing diffusion-based planners still struggle to reliably satisfy geometric feasibility in unseen cluttered environments with complex obstacle layouts. To address this challenge, we propose GeoSDF-Diff, a geometry-aware diffusion planner that incorporates multi-scale SDF conditioning into trajectory denoising. The key idea is to provide the denoiser with both route-level geometric context and fine local clearance evidence, enabling generated trajectories to better adapt to unseen complex obstacle layouts. Specifically, a Geometric Encoder extracts multi-scale SDF features and injects them into a DiT-X denoiser through cross-attention. We further introduce a trajectory-level training objective that combines SDF clearance, violation emphasis, smoothness, and path-length regularization, so that local infeasibilities are penalized during training rather than corrected only at inference time. Experiments on held-out cluttered environments show that, without post-hoc trajectory repair or sampling-time guidance, GeoSDF-Diff achieves a 65.2% average success rate across diverse test scenarios, outperforming strong diffusion baselines by 25.4% to 28.5%.

papers.title: Efficient Analysis of Numerous Galactic Compact Binaries via the Free-bin Scheme
papers.abstract: Global analysis of Galactic compact binaries (GCBs) for space-based gravitational-wave detectors is computationally demanding in the high-frequency region (above $\sim$10 mHz), where resolvable signals are sparse but frequency samples are numerous. We propose a free-bin scheme that evaluates the nontrivial likelihood only in movable frequency windows centered on sampled signal frequencies. The method preserves the joint-likelihood structure by replacing only the signal-containing regions of a precomputed null likelihood, and avoids the fixed-bin edge effect by construction because the windows follow the sampled frequencies. In a simulated TianQin dataset containing 193 GCBs, 192 injected sources are recovered with waveform fitting factors above 0.99. Numerical comparisons demonstrate that the free-bin and conventional full-band likelihood implementations yield identical results when the same finite-length local waveforms and numerical settings are used. Computational benchmarks show that the acceleration is primarily controlled by the fraction of the frequency domain covered by the merged signal windows and decreases as this coverage increases.

papers.title: Gumbel Substitution: Removing Sampler Drift from RL Without Trusting the Sampler
papers.abstract: When RL rollouts come from untrusted samplers on arbitrary hardware, precision and checkpoint lag, the sampling distribution $q$ differs from the trainer's policy $p$, and training on the sampler's tokens adds a drift term equal to supervised fine-tuning toward $q$. Published corrections (TIS, MIS, IcePop, score centering, GSPO, CISPO) all need $q(y)$, which a permissionless sampler reports and can misreport. We introduce Gumbel substitution. The coordinator fixes public Gumbel noise for every token position, bit-identical across GPUs, and the sampler draws $y=\arg\max(\ell^q+G)$. The trainer recomputes $v^*=\arg\max(\ell^p+G)$, the token its own policy would have drawn with the same noise, and scores $v^*$ in the sampler's context. For a sampler that follows the protocol, $v^*$ is an exact sample from $p$ given the prefix, so the drift vanishes in expectation for any $q$, without sampler-reported probabilities. We measure the residual left by the deployed heads, bound the one added by admission gates, and state what an adaptive sampler can still do. The same comparison gives a per-token match rate that admits and pays samplers. In the lab, on a 9B model with the same head on both sides, the expected drift of uncorrected training is at least 170 to 4,800 times that of substitution. On a 2B model under strong mismatch, uncorrected training collapses while substitution stays stable, comparable to MIS with score centering given the true $q$. On a permissionless network, a 9B model was trained for 158 optimizer steps on 15.75B tokens from heterogeneous samplers, with no skipped step and 1.21% of tokens substituted; it improved on all eight held-out benchmarks.

papers.title: Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation of RL Experts: Toward Continual Post-Training
papers.abstract: RL post-training typically produces domain experts that must then be consolidated into one model, and as new experts keep arriving, this consolidation becomes a continual process. Weight merging and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) must re-consolidate the whole model whenever an expert is added, and can erode capabilities outside the target domains. We propose Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation (CSPD), which keeps the pre-RL model frozen, distills each RL expert independently into a soft prompt, and composes experts by concatenating their prompts without joint training. A single soft prompt suffices to distill an RL expert, recovering at least 90% of the teacher's gain in 22 of 23 math, code, and agent settings. Independently trained prompts compose well. In a multi-expert setting, the average rises with every expert added, and the full composition matches MOPD (67.83 vs. 67.79). The composition generalizes best across six held-out benchmarks. Input-space adaptation adds little serving overhead, keeping throughput within 1.5% of the unadapted backbone and reaching 2.40x that of rank-4 LoRA. These results point toward continual post-training on a fixed backbone.

papers.title: HR-Merge: Model Merging with Headroom-Weighted Residual Refinement
papers.abstract: Model merging combines experts fine-tuned from a shared backbone, such as LoRA adapters of a large language model, into one multi-task model without further training. Existing methods apply one rule to every task, yet the accuracy they lose is uneven across tasks. We show that the lost accuracy remains recoverable from each task's residual, its task vector minus the merged update, and that a task's validation headroom, the share of its expert validation accuracy the merge loses, indicates where recovery pays off. Residuals from different tasks interfere, so they must be merged rather than summed. We propose HR-Merge, a training-free wrapper around any merging method. It weights each residual by its task's headroom, re-merges the weighted residuals with the base operator, and adds the result back at a strength selected on validation, falling back to the base merge when no strength helps. On six NLI adapters of LLaMA-3 8B, HR-Merge lifts TIES from 93.29 to 94.29 normalized accuracy, above all tested bases, mainly by recovering its weakest task. In vision, on three CLIP backbones, up to 20 tasks, and LoRA merging, it generally improves or preserves base accuracy and yields the best model in every setting.

papers.title: Pairing and modular: Generalized electrons and quasiholes inside the $\boxtimes$ of topological orders
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between the pair creation mechanism in physics and the pairing ($\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}$) in mathematics, focusing on the modular and algebraic properties. We provide a way to couple two topologically ordered systems, $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{A'}$ sharing the common (non-group-like) structure $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}=\overline{\mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}}$, through the nonabelian anyon analog of the pair creation mechanism denoted as $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}=\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}\boxtimes \mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}$. We identify $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the generalized version of electron operators in general topological orders or hidden current with (half-)integer spin involving the conformal embeddings. We provide a way to construct $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the hidden topological operator and identify $\mathbf{A}\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}\mathbf{A'}$, a general class of topoloical orders, as the $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$-extended symmetry topological field theory. We also conjecture a series of underlying (unexplored) modular invariants, connecting the conformal embedding and the pairing.

papers.title: A Lightweight Method for Validating Simulated LiDAR Configurations Based on Point Density over Distance
papers.abstract: Simulated LiDAR sensors play a crucial role in validating autonomous systems, yet achieving signal-level realism remains challenging due to simplified sensor models and limited configurability in common simulation environments. This paper presents a lightweight, platform-agnostic method to assess one observable aspect of LiDAR simulation fidelity: the range-dependent point density on annotated objects. The method uses only 3D bounding boxes and point clouds and does not require semantic labels, detailed maps, simulator internals, or perception models. To quantify agreement between real and simulated range-dependent point distributions, we formulate the Density Similarity Score (DSS), a bounded similarity representation derived from the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) over discretized distance bins. The method is evaluated against a real-world LiDAR using three CARLA configurations of varying complexity. Results show that naive parameter matching based on sensor datasheets leads to systematic point-density deviations, particularly in the near field, while a custom configuration using the sensor's non-uniform vertical beam angles achieves the highest similarity in the evaluated scenario (DSS: 0.559--0.709). The proposed approach is intended as an early-stage, signal-level consistency check for identifying gross mismatches in simulated LiDAR configurations. It should be interpreted as a complementary validation step rather than a complete measure of simulation quality or downstream perception performance.

papers.title: A Combinatorial Construction of Symmetric Magic Squares of Order Four
papers.abstract: We construct all symmetric nonnegative integer matrices of order four having a common sum on every row, column, and both diagonals. The construction is a disjoint union of twelve translates of free submonoids, each with five uniquely determined nonnegative integer parameters.Twelve is the smallest possible number of classes among finite disjoint unions of translates of free submonoids generated by five elements, even when generators outside the Hilbert basis are allowed. A comparison-based case analysis supplies integer inverse formulas and assigns every point on the shared faces to exactly one class. The normal forms prove that the twelve primitive extreme-ray generators form the entire Hilbert basis: eight have magic sum two and four have magic sum four. We exhibit the underlying regular unimodular triangulation and a single perturbation direction producing all half-open boundary conventions. The resulting positive multivariate generating function specializes to an explicit rational function and a quasipolynomial of period four in the magic sum. A further consequence is a reflexive lattice polytope associated with positive symmetric magic squares.

papers.title: VMSA: Video Memory Skill Agent for Long Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Long-video question answering requires retrieving and integrating relevant evidence from videos spanning hours or even days. Recent agentic approaches organize video information into external memories and iteratively retrieve evidence to answer questions. However, effective retrieval and reasoning remain challenging, as agents must determine what information to search for, which memory sources to access, and how to connect evidence across distant temporal intervals. To address these challenges, we propose Video Memory Skill Agent (VMSA), a framework that jointly designs structured video memories and memory skills for long-video understanding. VMSA constructs three complementary memory components. Segment Caption Memory and Entity Event Memory serve as searchable evidence sources, while Entity-Aware Episode Memory provides broad yet detailed video context to guide evidence retrieval and reasoning. To further support effective memory utilization, VMSA induces memory skills from successful agent trajectories, incrementally refining or extending a compact skill library to guide iterative evidence retrieval, reasoning, and verification. Across seven long-video question-answering benchmarks, VMSA achieves the highest accuracy on all three week-long egocentric benchmarks, outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 9.4% on Ego-R1 Bench, and the best or competitive performance on four additional benchmarks. Ablation studies further demonstrate the contributions of all three memory components and memory skills, with memory skills also improving temporal evidence localization.

papers.title: A Structured Levenberg--Marquardt Method for Binary Tensor Completion
papers.abstract: We develop a structured Levenberg--Marquardt (LM) method with trust-region globalization for binary tensor completion, using triple decomposition and a logistic loss. Under a local component-residual error bound and positive outer curvature, we prove quadratic convergence of the exact iteration for damping exponents $1\leδ\le2$, without requiring full row rank. A constant-rank criterion and an explicit rank-one certificate provide sufficient conditions for the residual error bound. The analysis decomposes the local error into outer-loss linearization, factor linearization, and regularization contributions. For a symmetric nonquadratic logistic--LSE family with $δ=2$, cancellation improves the objective-model error to fourth order and the decrease-ratio error to second order. A synthetic experiment illustrates the local quadratic convergence rate. On the HCP and Enron datasets, the proposed method improves binary tensor completion accuracy while requiring fewer outer iterations than the first-order methods.

papers.title: PanoUAV-Track: Full-Spherical UAV Visual Tracking in the Wild
papers.abstract: Existing UAV tracking benchmarks predominantly rely on perspective cameras with limited fields of view. Omnidirectional cameras enable full-spherical observation, yet tracking from moving UAV platforms remains largely unexplored. Unlike ground-level panoramic tracking, UAV-mounted omnidirectional cameras observe targets across both azimuth and elevation, introducing geometric challenges under equirectangular projection (ERP). To investigate this setting, we capture approximately \textbf{40 hours of real-world 8K panoramic UAV video} and construct \textbf{PanoUAV-Track} through temporal clip extraction, target annotation, and the integration of simulated sequences. The resulting benchmark comprises 1,895 sequences, 507,961 frames, and 2,872 annotated objects, covering real-world daytime and nighttime scenes alongside simulation, and supporting both visual and language-based target specification. Through extensive evaluations, we reveal a clear \textbf{perspective-to-spherical} generalization gap and identify tracking degradation associated with latitude-dependent distortion and ERP seam discontinuity. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{PanoUAV-Tracker (PUTrack)}, a geometry-aware tracking framework combining latitude-adaptive search and seam-aware periodic sampling. PUTrack improves zero-shot and in-domain tracking, particularly for seam-crossing targets. Code and benchmark resources will be available\footnote{\textcolor{tabpink}{https://libingyu01.github.io/PanoUAV-Track/}}.

papers.title: Frustration-Stabilized Hexamerons and Their Topological Magnons in Janus MXene
papers.abstract: Frustrated magnets on triangular lattices favour noncollinear order, and when inversion symmetry is broken they can host localized topological textures on top of that order. Here we show that the Janus MXene MnHf2C2FI is such a system. Combining first-principles calculations with atomistic spin simulations, we find that magnetism is confined to the Mn layer, where a strong antiferromagnetic nearest-neighbor exchange together with a sizable Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction stabilizes a frustrated 120 Neel ground state. On top of this ground state we identify a metastable hexameron: a composite of six merons and antimerons, one vortex-antivortex pair on each of the three sublattices, whose sublattice-resolved topological charges compensate. Linear spin-wave theory confirms that the hexameron is a local energy minimum, and its noncoplanar cores act as potential wells that bind discrete in-gap magnon modes below the bulk continuum. In a periodic hexameron array the magnon bands carry nonzero Chern numbers, and the resulting Berry curvature produces a magnon thermal Hall response whose sign depends on which of the two time-reversal partners of the hexameron is realized. Our results establish Janus MXenes as a two-dimensional platform in which frustration, broken inversion symmetry, and spin-orbit coupling combine to produce metastable antiferromagnetic solitons with distinct spectroscopic and transport fingerprints.

papers.title: Very weak solutions of nonlinear elliptic systems with Orlicz growth
papers.abstract:
In this work we consider non-linear elliptic equations with respect to Orlicz growth, for instance equations of the form $$ \mathrm{div}(\varphi(\vert 
abla u \vert) 
abla u)= 0. $$ We study very weak solutions to this system, that is, solutions that are not a priori in the correct energy space to this equation ($\varphi(\vert 
abla u \vert) \vert 
abla u \vert^2 \in L^1$). On the one hand, using rather mild assumptions on the corresponding Orlicz space (we need either the $Δ_2$ or $
abla_2$ condition, but not both at the same time), we can show that the integrability of very weak solutions improves to the energy space, provided that the initial integrability is close enough to the energy space. On the other hand, mirroring the construction of Colombo and Tione (Non-classical solutions of the $p$-Laplace equation, J. Eur. Math. Soc., 2024), for the $p$-Laplacian, we give a construction of 'wild' solutions for a $L \log L$-type Laplacian.

papers.title: Pushy Random Walk on the Bethe lattice: a Galton-Watson perspective
papers.abstract: Pushy random walks are minimal models of transport in deformable media, in which the walker displaces the obstacles it bumps into rather than being blocked by them. On the Bethe lattice, we show that the walkable structure dynamically created by a pushy walker can be generated a priori as an explicit multi-type Galton-Watson tree, so that the walker reduces to a simple random walk on a static random tree, and its escape to infinity coincides with the survival of the underlying branching process. Standard generating-function tools then give direct access to the escape properties of these walks. For the Sokoban walk, which pushes a single obstacle, we recover the known critical density $ρ_c = 1-(z-1)^{-2}$ and the behavior of the escape probability close to $ρ_c$, and derive its small-density asymptotics. For the second-order pushy walk, which can push trains of two obstacles, we establish the conjectured $ρ_c = 1-(z-1)^{-3}$, and compute the escape probability at all densities. Beyond escape, the same framework yields the statistics of the trace of trapped walkers: the distribution of the maximal depth follows from the extinction probabilities, while the distributions of the visited volume and of the number of dead ends are encoded in explicit functional equations for their generating functions, which we invert numerically. All predictions agree with Monte Carlo simulations.

papers.title: Finite Angular Derivative Sets and Almost Isometries of the Hyperbolic Disc
papers.abstract: We prove that a subset $E$ of the unit circle is the set of points at which an analytic self-map of the unit disc has a finite angular derivative if and only if $E$ is an $F_σ$ set. We also prove that, for every countable dense subset $E$ of the unit circle, there exists an almost isometry in the sense of Garnett--Papadimitrakis whose angular derivative is finite precisely on $E$.

papers.title: What Stays in the Picture? From Redundant Instructions to Dependency-Aware Image Editing
papers.abstract: We introduce complex redundant-instruction image editing, where a single request specifies multiple objects, their attributes, and spatial relations while revising or canceling earlier editing requirements. Direct editing can fail to recover this intent, while splitting the request into successive steps can preserve obsolete edits and visual errors. Our key insight is to resolve the revision history into a final editing target that jointly guides planning and verification, so that obsolete requests do not become visual edits. Based on this insight, CRIE-Agent learns to consolidate revisions into object-level final intent and executes the retained objects in reference-first blocks, establishing referenced objects before their dependents. Verification then guides complete re-execution from the source image, with conditional layout hints, preventing visual errors from failed attempts from being carried into subsequent ones. We also construct CRIE-S, a benchmark containing 10,000 complex and redundant editing instructions with exact final intent annotations. Across five image-editing backends on CRIE-S, CRIE-Agent raises complete editing success from 0% under direct editing to 27.5--50.0%.

papers.title: Beyond What They Say: Cue Acknowledgment and Robustness in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Explanations are used to assess whether vision-language models rely on visual evidence or misleading suggestions. A response that explicitly names a cue can still follow it, making disclosure alone an incomplete basis for judging robustness. We ask whether greater cue acknowledgment accompanies greater resistance. We compare matched answers and explanations under helpful, misleading, and conflicting visual and textual cues while holding the underlying question and correct answer fixed. A paired comparison shows that a model can select the endorsed wrong answer more often while acknowledging the cues more often. Reduced silence therefore need not indicate improved resistance. Explanations may also mention a textual suggestion while omitting an accompanying visual cue. Requesting evidence and acknowledgment does not consistently improve resistance in the tested settings. Outcomes vary across models and settings, and these comparisons do not isolate a causal effect of acknowledgment. Evaluations should report cue following and acknowledgment on the same instances, distinguishing visual from textual cues.

papers.title: Evidence sufficiency assessment enables cost-effective review allocation in on-premise clinical AI agents
papers.abstract: On-premise clinical AI agents must auto-accept high-confidence diagnoses, deferring others to clinician review, yet token probabilities and self-reported confidence miss errors, while more reliable five-run consistency incurs fivefold compute. We propose training-free decision-point evidence sufficiency assessment and a three-tier sequential triage protocol. Masking reasoning and diagnosis, the same 4B model scores sufficiency from objective evidence via prior-debiased probabilities over five ordered levels. Calibration freezes a nominal top-50% threshold, selecting single-run, five-run consistency, or full-deferral tiers by whether the one-sided 95% Wilson lower confidence bound of pass rate among accepted cases meets the 95% clinical target line. Across 1,605 MIRA-v2, CDM, VivaBench, and in-hospital liver malignancy primary cohort cases, MIRA-v2 single-run top-50% pass rate reached 98.91%, matching five-run consistency, saving ~80% compute; CDM achieved 96.00% test attainment by escalating to the five-run consistency tier; cross-specialty, missing-imaging, and combined enriched cohorts entered the full-deferral tier, capping calibration false-certification rate at 0.00%-3.50%.

papers.title: Pure Orbitronics: Hall Responses and Torques by Orbital Exchange in Spinless Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides
papers.abstract: Recent studies have identified orbital exchange fields as a novel mechanism for controlling electronic and magnetic phenomena through the orbital degree of freedom. In contrast to conventional spin exchange fields, orbital exchange fields couple directly to orbital angular momentum and can emerge from purely orbital interactions or dynamically through couplings to chiral excitations such as phonons and magnons. Motivated by these developments, we investigate the transport and torque responses generated by orbital exchange fields in two-dimensional materials.
